summary_short: Revenue of $531.8M rose 19.3% y/y but fell 15.4% q/q; net income swung to a $8.0M profit from a $142.7M year-ago loss, though it dropped 89.5% sequentially from $76.2M.
summary_long: Revenue of $531.8M grew 19.3% y/y but fell 15.4% q/q. Gross margin expanded to 62.7% (+25.3ppt y/y, +6.3ppt q/q) while operating margin rose to 34.6% (+37.9ppt y/y, +2.8ppt q/q), lifting operating income to $184.0M, up from a year-ago loss though down 8.0% sequentially. EBITDA of $190.3M similarly swung positive from a year-ago loss but fell 17.3% q/q. Net income of $8.0M reversed a $142.7M year-ago loss but dropped 89.5% q/q as net margin compressed to 1.5% from 12.1% last quarter. Cash rose to $966.1M (+15.4% y/y, +11.2% q/q); shareholders' equity grew to $1,489.3M (+21.6% y/y, +6.8% q/q).

drivers.explanation: FY2026 (full year, not Q4-isolated) revenue rose 9% on higher brokerage fee income and a swing to a net trading-securities gain; the filing gives no cause specific to this quarter alone.
Annual fee-and-commission mix shifted toward higher-margin brokerage services (+17% y/y) while net insurance revenue fell 30% on a regulatory commission cap; no Q4-isolated margin driver is given.
FY2026 net gain on trading securities of $158.8M (vs a $57.8M loss in FY2025) was the disclosed annual driver of the swing to profit; no standalone Q4 explanation is given.

FY2026 net income of $153.3M (full year, vs $76.2M in FY2025) reflects the trading-securities swing above, partly offset by a higher 32.1% effective tax rate after a Kazakhstan tax-law change; no Q4-specific driver given.
Sequential margin compression follows mechanically from the net-income decline against a smaller revenue base; not addressed separately in the release for Q4 alone.
FY2026 cash growth reflects a $770.4M rise in bank customer deposits and $783.5M of net debt issuance, partly offset by $1,049.2M used in investing activities; full-year, not Q4-isolated.
Growth driven by FY2026 net income of $153.3M, a $54.0M foreign-currency translation gain from tenge appreciation, and $68.0M of stock compensation expense; annual, not Q4-isolated.

Source is the FY2026 annual 10-K; the filer does not break out standalone Q4 figures or drivers, so the causal detail above is inferred from full fiscal-year (Apr 2025-Mar 2026) disclosures only, not the isolated quarter.
